teams.heading: Fiji's deaf national rugby sevens teams face $70,000 funding shortfall
teams.body: Fiji’s men’s and women’s deaf national rugby sevens teams are scrambling to raise up to $70,000 to secure their travel to the World Deaf Rugby Sevens Championship in Tokyo. Despite receiving grants from the Fiji National Sports Commission and the Australian High Commission’s PacificAus Sports programme, team manager Lionel Danford confirmed a significant financial deficit remains. Players, many of whom are currently unemployed, have been covering their own training travel expenses. The squad recently entered camp in Sigatoka ahead of the tournament, which starts later this month.

lead.why: The deaf national rugby sevens teams are facing a critical $70,000 funding deficit ahead of their upcoming World Championship campaign.

teams.heading: England Test duo Marcus Smith and Fin Baxter near injury returns
teams.body: Harlequins head coach Jason Gilmore has confirmed that England fly-half Marcus Smith is back on the training pitch after recovering from a broken finger. Smith, who has been sidelined since pre-season, is currently on track for a return to competitive action. Meanwhile, loosehead prop Fin Baxter is also nearing availability following long-term foot injury setbacks. Gilmore noted, "He's on track at the moment," regarding Smith, adding that both players could potentially return to the selection mix for upcoming club fixtures.

lead.why: The return of key England Test players Marcus Smith and Fin Baxter provides a significant update for the national setup.

teams.heading: Victor Wembanyama credits Provence Rugby for inspiring team spirit and camaraderie
teams.body: NBA superstar Victor Wembanyama has highlighted the positive impact of his recent training stint with the Top 14 hopefuls Provence Rugby. The 22-year-old basketball player spent his off-season working with the second-tier squad, participating in line-out drills and physical conditioning. Wembanyama noted he was "inspired" by the club’s atmosphere, praising the genuine welcome he received from the players and staff. Provence have started their domestic campaign strongly, remaining unbeaten in their first five league matches as they pursue promotion.

teams.heading: Rugby brain injury legal action faces continued threat of financial collapse
teams.body: The ongoing legal action against World Rugby and other governing bodies regarding concussion-related brain injuries remains in a precarious position. Claimants are currently facing a £2.8m legal bill to continue their case, a significant hurdle that threatens the litigation's survival. While these bodies recently lost a battle to have the cases thrown out of court, as reported in August, the financial burden continues to place the future of these claims in doubt as both sides navigate this complex dispute.

lead.why: The legal action regarding rugby brain injury liabilities remains a significant unresolved matter for the sport's governing bodies and players.

teams.heading: Italy maintain attacking output despite difficult results in recent window
teams.body: In their last 11 international matches, the Azzurri have scored a total of 190 points, averaging 17.3 points per game. Conversely, they have conceded 318 points in that same window, an average of 28.9 per fixture. Amidst these challenges, the side recorded their most significant margin of victory by defeating Chile 34-19 at home during the November 2025 international window. This remains their standout result in terms of points scored and winning margin over the last 11 tests.

teams.heading: Scottish Rugby and Scottish Gas launch new community clubhouse fund
teams.body: Scottish Rugby and Principal Partner Scottish Gas have launched the Energy for Tomorrow Fund to assist clubs in upgrading their facilities. The initiative offers up to £20,000 in matched funding for projects designed to improve energy efficiency and reduce long-term running costs. Following a specialist retrofit survey, successful clubs will receive support to manage crowdfunding campaigns for their site upgrades. The programme aims to support up to 5 clubs annually for the next 3 years as part of a wider net-zero ambition.

lead.why: This story highlights a new community initiative launched by Scottish Rugby and Scottish Gas which has been formally announced in the latest reporting.

teams.heading: Marika Koroibete Debuts As Fetuli Paea Starts For Dragons In URC
teams.body: Marika Koroibete is set for his Ospreys debut this weekend as they face the Dragons at Rodney Parade in the United Rugby Championship. The Swansea-based side, winless after two fixtures in South Africa, have bolstered their backline with the Wallabies star. Meanwhile, the hosts have made three changes to their starting side following their victory over the Scarlets, with Tongan international Fetuli Paea named at outside centre for his first start of the campaign.

teams.heading: Argentina leads four-nation proposal to host the 2035 World Cup
teams.body: The Argentine Rugby Union has officially submitted all technical documentation required for the 2035 Rugby World Cup bid. Leading a joint effort alongside Uruguay, Chile, and Brazil, the union aims to showcase a region with a combined population of 283 million. Proposed venues include the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires and the Mario Alberto Kempes in Córdoba. The governing body will evaluate these infrastructure plans ahead of the final host decision, which is scheduled for determination by the World Rugby Council in 2027.

teams.heading: Japan Sakura XV end European tour winless following second Irish defeat
teams.body: The Japan Sakura XV conclude their European tour without a win after falling 19-43 to Ireland in Cork on 3 October. Despite a bright start—leading 7-0 through a Sakurako Korai try—the team struggled against Irish pack dominance and persistent kicking pressure. Head coach Toshizumi Kitagawa’s side now turns its attention to the WXV Global Series, where the squad is set to face Wales twice. Japan must address their set-piece inconsistencies to regain the form that previously defined their defensive line speed.

lead.why: It is the most significant recent result concerning a national Japanese squad, capturing the conclusion of their European tour.

teams.heading: Jeff Wilson identifies administrative costs as burden for New Zealand Rugby
teams.body: Former All Black Jeff Wilson has urged New Zealand Rugby to embrace private investment to relieve mounting financial pressure. Highlighting the fiscal challenges facing the national body, Wilson noted there are 470 rugby administrators in the country, a figure he described as an “astounding number” that adds a significant burden to the organisation’s budget. Wilson argues that reducing costs while maintaining quality is essential for the future of the game and the long-term viability of professional structures.

lead.why: This story addresses the structural financial sustainability of NZ Rugby, distinct from the match-specific news reported earlier.

teams.heading: Cam Roigard admits stinging frustration following three straight Springboks series defeats
teams.body: New Zealand scrum-half Cam Roigard has described the aftermath of the recent series against the Springboks as a period of persistent frustration. Despite the All Blacks looking dangerous in attack during the campaign, Roigard pointed to consistent failures in set-piece accuracy and discipline as the critical margins that allowed South Africa to secure three consecutive victories. Reflecting on the series, he admitted that the lack of adaptation against the world champions still stings, noting that the lessons remain unresolved as they look ahead.

lead.why: It highlights the lingering impact of the Springboks' recent series win on their rivals' internal confidence and perspective.
